text: The dashboard audit from Lesson 19 finds two real candidates: a consumer-lag alert averaged across all pods, and a secondary-cloud health check aggregating status across node pools. Both get the same per-dimension breakout the FinOps dashboard already received.

The Lesson 22 ceiling bump becomes a version-controlled Terraform change instead of a manual patch someone has to remember. topologySpreadConstraints becomes the default for every multi-replica deployment, and a PodDisruptionBudget is added so a node drain can't recreate the same imbalance a different way.
A budget anomaly alert is added specifically for the ceiling bump, so Dana's team sees the expected spend increase land exactly when it's supposed to, not discover it cold in next month's bill.

None of this counts as done yet. A runbook and a Terraform diff both describe intended behavior. Theo schedules a real game-day drill ahead of next season to prove it actually holds under a real failure condition.
